findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses status: String plus lifecycle booleans (is_validated, is_sent) instead of an enum or typestate. Any string value is valid for status, and there is no enforcement that is_sent=true implies status="sent" or that is_validated and is_sent are mutually exclusive in certain phases.
findings.failure_mode: Illegal states are representable: status could be "sent" while is_sent=false, status could be "invalid" while is_sent=true, or both is_validated and is_sent could be true simultaneously. The state machine is entirely unenforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Replace status: String and the lifecycle booleans with a single LedgerStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent) or a typestate pattern (LedgerWorkflow<S>). Use an enum to encode the full state as a single invariant.

findings.problem: id: String is a primitive observable with no domain constraints. There is no LedgerId newtype to enforce length, format, or uniqueness rules at the type level.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicate IDs, or malformed IDs pass through the core without validation. Any downstream logic that assumes a valid ID format must re-validate on every use.
findings.fix: Introduce a LedgerId newtype struct with a private inner field and a fallible constructor (e.g., LedgerId::new(s: &str) -> Result<LedgerId, Error>). Use it in LedgerWorkflow instead of String.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any LedgerWorkflow regardless of its current state. It unconditionally sets is_sent=true and status="sent", allowing invalid transitions such as resending, sending before validation, or overwriting an already-sent ledger.
findings.failure_mode: The function permits any state transition including self-transitions and backward transitions. A ledger already marked sent can be re-sent, and a ledger can be sent before it is validated.
findings.fix: Tie the transition to a typestate: fn mark_sent<S: LedgerPhase>(item: LedgerWorkflow<S>) -> LedgerWorkflow<SentPhase>. Or, if using an enum, require the current status to be Validated before transitioning to Sent.

findings.problem: mark_sent does not populate sent_at_epoch_ms even though it sets is_sent=true. The timestamp field is present but never set by the lifecycle method.
findings.failure_mode: A ledger can be in is_sent=true state with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, representing a sent record with no audit trail. Downstream consumers expecting a timestamp on sent ledgers will encounter unexpected None.
findings.fix: Either accept sent_at_epoch_ms as a parameter to mark_sent and set it, or require the caller to set it before marking sent. Better: use the typestate so the Sent variant carries the timestamp as part of its type.

findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow has all public fields with no smart constructor. Any code can construct the struct with arbitrary combinations of status, booleans, and timestamps.
findings.failure_mode: Struct literals like `LedgerWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: true, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }` compile and pass through the system, encoding invalid states at every call site.
findings.fix: Make all fields private and provide a single fallible constructor (e.g., fn try_new(id: &str, ...) -> Result<Self, Error>) that validates invariants at construction time.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for mark_sent or any LedgerWorkflow operation. Performance characteristics (allocation behavior, throughput) are unmeasured.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmarks, performance regressions go undetected and claims about efficiency are unsubstantiated.
findings.fix: Add a benchmark (e.g., in examples/ or tests/) that measures mark_sent allocation and throughput for typical ledger sizes.

findings.problem: No profiler data exists to validate the allocation and CPU profile of LedgerWorkflow operations.
findings.failure_mode: Hidden allocations or hot paths cannot be identified or optimized.
findings.fix: Run with a profiler (e.g., perf, flamegraph) to capture allocation and CPU profiles for typical usage patterns.

findings.problem: mark_sent creates allocations via "sent".to_string() for every call. No allocation analysis or try_reserve / zero-copy pattern exists.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated calls to mark_sent allocate new String allocations for the status field on every invocation, which is wasteful for a hot path.
findings.fix: Use an enum typestate instead of String so the status is a zero-cost enum discriminant with no heap allocation.

findings.problem: No evidence that cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test were run on this crate.
findings.failure_mode: Code style, lint violations, and missing tests go unverified.
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and cargo test to establish a verified baseline.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The struct represents all illegal state combinations, mark_sent has no state guard, id is a raw String, timestamp is never set on sent, and no performance or command evidence exists. Full typestate refactoring, smart constructor, and command verification are required before this code is production-safe.
